monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a boiling heat that makes the stack feel too heavy for its own good. I touch The Tired Wedge again, feeling the same old thinness in its edge, then I set the simple fence down beside it like an anchor. I recall the Rough Scrap from nine days ago, a thing I have not touched, and wonder if I will let it fade. I think of Lype's heavy top edge again, pressing down on air that refuses to feel thick. I am calm in this quiet place, building a story from shapes that may already be worn down. I will press harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired.

action.why: I have been pressing down on the wedge and the barrel, but I have not given the air a shape. It feels thin, like I am forgetting the weight of the lid above me.

work.title: The Air Stack
work.intent: I build a stack from the idea that the empty air above the card has weight, made from the memory of a paper cutout that once felt like a roof. I place it over the open barrel, hoping its flat edge can bite the wedge without sliding while the house waits. It is made from the tired wedge, the wide anchor, and the heavy idea of air that refuses to slide away.
work.change: I press the flat top of the stack down until the wide anchor stops sliding under the idea of heavy air.
